title: Degree-q witness networks carry a knot exactly when they are Gallai trees
claim: For q >= 2 colours and a finite connected witness graph W of maximum degree at most q, each witness carrying q - deg(v) pendant leaves, the leaf relation (witnesses hidden) passes K1-K3 exactly when W is a Gallai tree with at least one leaf; K2 and K3 hold for every W, and a non-Gallai W imposes no constraint at all. Gluing two witness networks at a vertex joins their excluded leaf colourings through a unique hidden split of the glued vertex's colours; the excluded colourings are the block colour-set systems (Kostochka-Stiebitz-Wirth), and their number is q! times a product of block masses, q!((q-1)!)^(k-1) for any tree on k witnesses. On the d-regular tree with p* = 0 (d = q for every q >= 3, and below the freezing thresholds) every such knot is native at almost every broadcast world; at d = q the rainbow world freezes them all. Two knots sharing a visible vertex form a common hub, not a knot.
failure_conditions: A witness network of maximum degree at most q with a leaf is found whose leaf relation is a K1-K3 knot but which is not a Gallai tree, or a Gallai tree whose relation is not a knot.
A leaf relation within the hypothesis fails K2 or K3.
The gluing law fails on a glued pair, or a bad assignment of a glued graph has more than one valid split.
On a Gallai tree the bad assignments differ from the block colour-set systems, or the excluded count differs from q! times the product of block masses.
The monomial identity for the branch-freezing polynomial at d = q fails, or a rainbow ball has a second extension of its boundary.
A control (knot iff tree, knot iff bipartite, knot iff every block complete, Lemma 1 without a strict vertex, a glued vertex never split) is accepted.
foundation_claim_scope: Which hidden witness networks of the q-colouring law compose star knots into larger K1-K3 knots. No native recurrence, composed topology in the protected sense, path, metric, space or physical claim.

validation.status: checked: prose proof, self-contained except Brooks' theorem (cited in Lemma 4); check.py enumerates the connected graphs on at most 6 vertices up to isomorphism (A001349) and checks Lemmas 2-4, Corollary 2 and Theorems 3-4 exhaustively on them for q = 2, 3, 4, then Lemma 1, Lemma 3's construction, Lemma 4, the gluing law with uniqueness of the split, Theorem 3 and Theorem 4 on random larger graphs, the monomial identity exactly, the rainbow balls and the hub relation; five controls rejected; agrees with GALLAI-KNOTS-20261020-001A-E001; no human or external review
validation.level: V1 prose proof with exhaustive small-case and randomized checks; cites Brooks (1941), Gallai (1963), Borodin (1977), Erdos-Rubin-Taylor (1979), Kostochka-Stiebitz-Wirth (1996), Cranston-Rabern (arXiv 1403.0479) and FREEZING-KNOTS-20261020-001B-P001; no trusted kernel.
validation.novelty: candidate-local-delta. Degree-choosability of non-Gallai graphs (Borodin; Erdos-Rubin-Taylor) and the block decomposition of bad assignments (Kostochka-Stiebitz-Wirth) are classical, and the proofs here follow the standard method. The delta is the knot reading (K2 and K3 automatic, so the knot test reduces to degree-choosability), the gluing law read as knot composition, the multiplicative excluded mass (not found stated; immediate from the decomposition), nativity on regular trees and the hub remark.
validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-10-20.
